2607.29602.title: FriendBench: Benchmarking Dyadic Familiarity Inference in Humans and Multimodal Large Language Models
2607.29602.paper_summary: Reading a social situation often depends on behavior, not words alone. We introduce FriendBench, a benchmark for inferring whether two people are already familiar or are meeting as strangers, from a 20-second clip of a dyadic ice-breaker conversation. Every pair answers the same type of prompt, so only the manner of interaction can reveal the answer. Across text, audio, and video, we compare 26 models from seven companies against matched human panels over 96 balanced dyads. The best model and the human crowd are statistically indistinguishable on accuracy in every modality, but reach it differently: humans stay balanced across the two answers, while the strongest models lean toward "stranger"---a difference in effective prior, not discrimination. Richer channels help both unequally, and only humans gain from visible behavior on top of speech. We release the stimuli, human ratings, and model predictions.
2607.29602.paper_summary_zh: 閱讀社交情境往往依賴於行為，而不僅僅是言語。我們介紹了FriendBench，一個基準，用於推斷兩個人是否已經熟悉或是作為陌生人見面，這基於一段20秒的雙人破冰對話片段。每對參與者回答相同類型的提示，因此只有互動的方式能揭示答案。在文本、音頻和視頻中，我們比較了來自七家公司26個模型，與96對平衡的雙人組進行匹配的人類小組進行比較。在每種模式下，最佳模型和人類群體在準確性上統計上無法區分，但達到的方式不同：人類在兩個答案之間保持平衡，而最強的模型則傾向於「陌生人」——這是一種有效先驗的差異，而非歧視。更豐富的通道對兩者的幫助不均，並且只有人類在言語之上從可見行為中獲益。我們發布了刺激材料、人類評分和模型預測。
